podcast.title: Polaris Music Prize Win (2006)
podcast.body: Final Fantasy, the project of Owen Pallett, received the Polaris Music Prize in its inaugural year, 2006, for the album "He Poos Clouds." This win generated controversy, as the prize aims to reward musical excellence without regard for genre or commercial success, leading to debate about its lasting impact compared to other nominated albums. "When the winning album was, he poos clouds. Yeah, great title. By Final Fantasy, the vehicle for one time arcade fire violinist Owen Palette, which won out over records by Broken Social Scene, The New Prenogpers, and Metric."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Polaris Music Prize Nomination (2006)
xref.body: Broken Social Scene was among the artists nominated for the inaugural Polaris Music Prize in 2006, but their album ultimately lost to Final Fantasy's "He Poos Clouds." "The winning album was... By Final Fantasy... which won out over records by Broken Social Scene, The New Prenogpers, and Metric."

xref.title: Polaris Music Prize Nomination (2006)
xref.body: The New Pornographers were nominated for the first Polaris Music Prize in 2006, where their record was considered alongside others but did not win, with Final Fantasy taking the prize. "The winning album was... By Final Fantasy... which won out over records by Broken Social Scene, The New Prenogpers, and Metric."

xref.title: Polaris Music Prize Nomination (2006)
xref.body: Metric was one of the bands nominated for the 2006 Polaris Music Prize, an award aimed at recognizing artistic merit over commercial success, though the prize was ultimately awarded to Final Fantasy. "The winning album was... By Final Fantasy... which won out over records by Broken Social Scene, The New Prenogpers, and Metric."
